obligation: Banking organization notification incident (bank)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, the bank's operations or services to a material portion of customers, or a business line whose failure would cause material loss (determination recorded with date and time)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident has occurred
notify: OCC supervisory office or OCC-designated point of contact (email, telephone, or other method the OCC prescribes)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - national bank (53.1(c)). A BEC fraud against one customer is usually not a notification incident; escalate if bank mailboxes, the admin console, or many customers are affected. Decision by the ISO and the President and CEO

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (holding company)
trigger: Notification incident that affects Cris Santos Company, the bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the holding company determines a notification incident has occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a bank notification incident also affects the holding company; decide at the same time as the OCC determination

obligation: Bank service provider notice to the bank (inbound)
trigger: Provider determines a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, covered services to the bank for four or more hours (not scheduled maintenance)
deadline: As soon as possible after the provider's determination
notify: Bank-designated point of contact (ISO and COO shared mailbox and phone); if none was given, the CEO and CIO or comparable officers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty of the core processor, digital banking provider, and card processor. Designated contacts to be sent by 2026-09-30 (P03 G-041)

obligation: Regulator notice of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A II.A.1.b (guidance)
trigger: Bank becomes aware of an incident involving unauthorized access to or use of sensitive customer information (name, address, or phone with an account number or SSN; or a user name and password that allow access to an account)
deadline: As soon as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - an attacker using a customer's online banking user name and password is unauthorized access to sensitive customer information. Supplement A is interpretive guidance (should), examined as part of the response program

obligation: Customer notice under the response program
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A III.A to III.C (guidance)
trigger: Reasonable investigation shows misuse of the customer's information has occurred or is reasonably possible
deadline: As soon as possible; may be delayed only if law enforcement determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation and asks in writing
notify: Affected customers (clear and conspicuous notice with the content in Supplement A III.B, by mail and phone)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Compliance Officer decides and documents; in the BEC scenario misuse has occurred for the affected business customer

obligation: Suspicious activity report
trigger: Known or suspected federal criminal violation against the bank or through it: any amount for insider abuse; $5,000 or more with an identifiable suspect; $25,000 or more regardless of suspect
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection; up to 30 more days to identify a suspect, never more than 60 days after initial detection
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA/AML Officer. A fraudulent wire of $25,000 or more always requires a SAR. SAR existence is confidential (21.11(k))

obligation: Immediate notice of an ongoing violation
trigger: A reportable violation that needs immediate attention, such as an ongoing fraud
deadline: Immediately, by telephone, in addition to the timely SAR
notify: Appropriate law enforcement authority and the OCC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker is still active (for example, more fraudulent wire requests or continued online banking sessions)

obligation: Board notice of SAR filing
trigger: A SAR is filed
deadline: Promptly after filing
notify: Board of Directors or the committee it designates (Audit and Risk Committee)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA/AML Officer reports at the next committee meeting or sooner

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; fast reporting improves the chance of freezing funds
notify: FBI through ic3.gov; local FBI field office for large losses
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but part of POL-03 4.7; supports the SAR and any law enforcement delay request

obligation: Wire recall request to the beneficiary bank
citation: Payment system practice; funds transfer agreement (contract)
trigger: A wire the bank sent is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery; before the beneficiary bank releases funds
notify: Beneficiary bank (phone to its wire or fraud department, followed by a written request); Federal Reserve payment services message where available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Deposit Operations Manager. Not a legal notice, but the most time-critical step

obligation: Refund of an unauthorized payment order
trigger: A payment order accepted in the customer's name is not authorized and is not effective as the customer's order, for example because the bank did not follow the agreed security procedure (callback)
deadline: Refund with interest from the date the bank received payment; counsel determines effectiveness under 670.202
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida law governs the funds transfer agreement. Counsel decides; the skipped callback is central to the analysis

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information of a Florida individual (includes a user name with a password that permits access to an online account, and an account number with a required access code or password)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; notice under the primary federal regulator's rules or guidelines is deemed compliant
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an individual's personal information was accessed (for example, the business customer's authorized online banking user). Counsel confirms; the Supplement A customer notice can meet the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: Bank decides notice is not required because, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the bank relies on the no-harm exception; not expected in the BEC scenario because financial harm occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: No for a single-customer BEC; yes if the incident grows to 500 or more Florida individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No for a single-customer BEC; yes above 1,000

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected individuals

obligation: Financial institution bond and cyber insurance notice
trigger: Loss or suspected loss from fraud or a security incident
deadline: Per policy; notify the carrier before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. The CFO holds the policies

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not in a BEC incident (no ransom); kept for extortion scenarios (POL-03 4.8)

obligation: FDIC notification incident rule
trigger: Notification incident at an FDIC-supervised institution
deadline: 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's primary federal regulator is the OCC; the OCC rule (Part 53) applies instead

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the rule covers financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction; the bank is supervised by the OCC

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident and extortion payment
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity; extortion payment
deadline: 72 hours after determination; 24 hours after payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - not New York-chartered or licensed

obligation: SEC Reg S-P customer notification
trigger: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information at a broker-dealer, investment company, investment adviser, or transfer agent
deadline: No later than 30 days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: No - no SEC-registered broker-dealer or adviser in the group

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (as adopted by states)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - no insurance agency

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - neither the bank nor the holding company is an SEC registrant

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank holds no federal contracts
